newsitem.title: INDIA: India studying making rupee convertible -- minister.
newsitem.headline: India studying making rupee convertible -- minister.

text.p: The Indian government is studying the possibility of making the rupee fully convertible, but foreign exchange reserves would have to rise first, Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah was quoted on Monday as saying.

The Press Trust of India quoted Ramaiah as telling a conference in the southern city of Hyderabad on Sunday that the government would take a decision soon on whether to make the rupee fully convertible on the capital account.
"We are seriously thinking about how soon we should go in for full convertibility," Ramaiah was quoted as saying. "Once foreign exchange reserves improve further, it will be done."
The commerce minister also said the government had decided to modify the Foreign Exchange Regulations Act (FERA) in response to demands for its review.
